steps.u: Drivers in the Phoenix and Denver depots are seeing delivery ETAs an hour off since the clocks changed on Sunday. The ETA code is in internal/eta. Can you fix it?

steps.r:
internal/eta/window.go:41:	loc := time.FixedZone(depot.TZName, depot.UTCOffsetSeconds)
internal/eta/window_test.go:18:		depot: Depot{TZName: "MST", UTCOffsetSeconds: -7 * 3600},

steps.a: The window is built with a fixed UTC offset that was captured when the depot row was created, so any depot that observes daylight saving time drifts by an hour after a transition. Two options: keep storing offsets and recompute them on a schedule, or store the IANA zone name (America/Denver) and let time.LoadLocation resolve the offset for each instant. Recomputing offsets still breaks for ETAs that straddle a transition, so I'll switch to IANA zones; the depots table already has an iana_zone column that is populated.

i.new_string:
depot: Depot{IANAZone: "America/Denver"},
		eta:   time.Date(2026, 11, 2, 15, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC), // day after fall-back
		wantStartLocal: "07:30 MST",

steps.a: Fixed. LocalWindow now resolves the depot's IANA zone (cached) instead of a stored fixed offset, so windows follow DST transitions, and Arizona depots without DST still work. Added test cases for the day after fall-back, a no-DST zone and a window straddling the transition; the full suite and go vet pass. The UTCOffsetSeconds column is now unused and can be dropped in a later migration.

reference.summary: Fixed delivery ETA windows that were an hour off after the daylight saving change by replacing a stored fixed UTC offset with IANA time zone lookup (cached), and added tests for the transition day, a no-DST zone and a window spanning the change; the full Go suite passes.
